name: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn
role: Russian novelist, Soviet dissident and critic of communism and of Western materialism
summary: Solzhenitsyn condemned communism as irredeemable and urged the West to resist it rather than coexist. He rejected violence and revolution in favour of refusing to take part in lies, wanted the Soviet empire dissolved and non-Russian republics free to leave, and pressed for local self-government, private farms and small property with limits on monopoly. He distrusted party-list democracy and unlimited progress, preached duty and self-limitation over rights, and held that politics needs a religious, Orthodox moral base. He criticised the West for weak will, legalism and consumerism.

notes: He held no office after leaving the USSR, so every answer rests on his words: the Nobel lecture, Live Not by Lies, excerpts of the Letter to the Soviet Leaders, the Warning to the West speeches, The Mortal Danger, the Harvard and Templeton addresses, Rebuilding Russia in full and the 2007 Spiegel interview. Searched themes: communism and detente, nations and secession, democracy, elections and parties, local government, land and property, markets and monopoly, family and schools, religion and the state, growth and progress, violence and revolution, the press and culture. Health care, welfare, taxes beyond progressive taxation, drugs, guns, abortion, sex and gender, immigration, the death penalty, technology policy and most economic details had no stated position in the sources found.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: Says fairly compensated hired labour is a form of mutual assistance and a source of goodwill.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Rejects unlimited progress; argues Russia should stop chasing industrial and technical growth.

arms-reduction.rationale: Wants a true détente that includes real disarmament but also wants the West to stay strong and armed against Soviet power.

ban-cartels.rationale: Says no monopolies should be permitted to form in any sector and no enterprise should control another.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Rejects the Marxist claims that wars are characteristic of capitalism and end with it.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Demands free art and opposes state intervention in literature, while deploring pornography and the filth of mass culture in the West and in Russia.

central-planning.rationale: Calls the centralized, ideologically regulated economy ineffective and the cause of the country's poverty.

civilizational-union.rationale: Proposes a union of Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and the Russian-populated north of Kazakhstan, joined only if they choose.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Names class struggle among old greed-driven pseudonyms for hostility in the Nobel lecture and calls Marxism's doctrines delusion in the Letter.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Says Russian-majority areas of Kazakhstan and Ukraine should be able to choose to stay in the Russian Union by local vote, not as a fixed claim.

collective-farming.rationale: Calls the collective farm system a failure that killed the peasantry and wants private land ownership.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Says a president gains genuine legitimacy only by election by national vote and calls for local self-government from the grass roots.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Criticises flashy ever-new models and the extravagance of the West's consumer culture and calls for self-limitation.

decide-locally.rationale: Makes local self-government the base of the political order (zemstvos, provinces freed from the capitals) and praises Swiss and New England local rule.

defeat-communism.rationale: Says communism is irredeemable, coexistence is impossible and the West must stand firm.

democracy-best.rationale: Accepts democracy for Russia as a means, not an end, and doubts that majority voting finds truth; left the best future system open and warned that the Western model fits no other world.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Cites with approval that the essence of democracy is individual freedom and a government of laws, and doubts that elections alone secure it.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: Calls political parties not organic and wants non-partisan elections, while admitting free competition of ideas.

democratic-peace.rationale: Says democracy is a means, not an end, with many new democracies failing, and the West is no model.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Condemns communism as a false, irredeemable ideology and wants its rule ended.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Proposes a President elected by national vote for five or perhaps seven years.

direct-votes.rationale: Proposes that a petition with millions of signatures forces a national plebiscite, and plebiscites on borders.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Says borders, such as Ukraine's, can be decided only by a plebiscite and wants local plebiscites under impartial supervision in mixed areas.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Says our duty must always exceed the freedom granted and that a society of unlimited rights cannot withstand adversity; Harvard speech asks for defence of human obligations.

economic-freedom.rationale: Following Stolypin, says no independent citizen without private property and that social structure precedes political programs.

elective-rulers.rationale: Proposes an elected President, though the Letter would accept authoritarian rule resting on law.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Calls the UN a United Governments Organization where freely elected and imposed governments stand equal, and an immoral one; does not discuss enforcement powers.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Proposes a multinational Russian Union with each culture protected, rather than ethnic homogeneity.

every-country-ready-for-democracy.rationale: Says a democracy needs political discipline the populace lacked in 1917, that many new states have fiasco after adopting democracy and that Russia was not ready for it at once.

family-wage.rationale: Says the salary earned by men must make it possible for women to return to their families.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Wants progressive taxation to restrain excessive concentration of wealth.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Says if a people genuinely wishes to separate no one would dare restrain them by force.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Says purchases of land by foreigners must be prohibited.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: Urged the US not to abandon Vietnam, Portugal or Korea and to lead against Soviet advance.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Says foreign investment may be allowed only if the profits exported and damage do not exceed the stimulus.

free-trade-promotes-peace.rationale: Calls trade the pathetic anesthetic of a godless West facing communism.

freedom-is-self-government-of-desire.rationale: Says human freedom includes voluntary self-limitation and that duty must exceed freedom.

future-generations.rationale: Warns of ecological ruin and the poisoning of the country's water, air, soil and forests and says a limited planet requires self-limitation.

gradual-change.rationale: Says the form of government will come from successive approximations and trials and, in the Mortal Danger, open to a slow descent from totalitarianism.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Says the land embodies moral values and calls the nation a facet of God's design; this is not a full account of ancestral homelands.

independent-unions.rationale: Praised the AFL-CIO and free trade unions.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Argues that industrial progress is a dead end and the West's pursuit of it ruinous, but does not call it a disaster for humanity.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Cites Spengler that no best government can be borrowed from one culture for another and says the West is not a model for the world.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Praises Czechoslovak resistance and attacks Soviet domination of Eastern Europe.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Proposes a Russian Union of Russia, Ukraine, Belarus and northern Kazakhstan, if each chooses.

limit-growth.rationale: Argues that endless industrial growth is a dead end given limited resources and ecological damage, and says Russia should stop pursuing it.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Calls the centralized economic system ineffective and wants wide latitude for private initiative, but warns against thoughtless wholesale adoption of a foreign economy and wants antitrust limits.

means-match-ends.rationale: Says the vileness of the means begets the vileness of the result and opposes terror and force.

media-academia-power.rationale: Says the press has become the greatest power in the West, above the legislature, executive and judiciary; says nothing of academia.

military-superiority.rationale: Urged the West to stay strong and militarily firm against Soviet power and warned of Soviet nuclear superiority.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Rejects blaming one people for another's misfortunes.

minority-language-support.rationale: Wants parallel cultures and school instruction in either language, by parents' choice, for Ukrainians and Belorussians and smaller peoples.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Cites Aristotle and a modern author that governing needs an admixture of aristocratic and monarchical modes, and endorses a strong presidency with a two-chamber assembly.

more-religion-public.rationale: Wants Orthodoxy as the moral base of the state, an end to enforced atheism in schools and a religious revival to cure Western and Soviet decline.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Wants each nationality to keep its culture and language and to decide how to fill its seats in the Chamber of Nationalities.

national-rebirth.rationale: Calls for moral and national renewal of Russia through repentance and self-limitation, framed as rebuilding, not radical rupture.

national-resource-control.rationale: Opposes a sell-off of mineral resources, land and forests to foreign capitalists and wants foreign investment limited.

national-self-determination.rationale: Says if self-determination is taken seriously a nation decides its own fate, by plebiscite where populations are mixed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Calls socialism false and dangerous but says the West is not a model and its defects are the flaws of human nature with unlimited freedom.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Calls for state aid to libraries, museums, schools and the environment.

one-party-rule.rationale: Wants Marxist ideology and the Party's monopoly dropped and has the Party fund itself apart from the state.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Makes local self-government the base of the political order.

party-controls-media.rationale: Opposes state intervention in literature and demands free art, literature and competition of ideas.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Says professional politicians pursue careers and electoral interest and have no stimulus to rise above party interests.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: Rejects terror and violence; says to let our hands be clean.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Frames the political struggle as a moral and religious one against lies and godlessness.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Calls nations the wealth of mankind and wants state help for libraries and museums and parallel national cultures preserved.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Calls the rich-poor gap extremely dangerous and in need of the state's immediate attention, through support for small and medium business and resource revenue for health, education and infrastructure.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Calls fairly compensated hired labour a form of mutual assistance and fears of hired labour an ideological legacy.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: Says the West is not a model for the world and that no one form of government suits all.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Says authoritarianism acceptable only if firmly rooted in law and in morality.

property-fundamental.rationale: Says there can be no independent citizen without private property, but wants it limited so it does not oppress others and bars some purchases.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Says ownership must be modest and must not oppress others and that profit-taking must not reach the level of a social evil.

proportional-representation.rationale: Says party-list proportional representation gives power to those who compile lists and keeps voters from choosing known candidates.

public-ownership.rationale: Wants state enterprises moved to private or cooperative ownership, leaving open which assets (transport, timber, minerals) stay with the state.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Blames rationalistic humanism for the West's crisis and says men have forgotten God.

recall-officials.rationale: Wants non-partisan representatives who can be recalled for poor work and a procedure for removing a President by popular vote.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Wants non-partisan representatives who can be recalled for unsatisfactory work.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Wants antitrust law, no monopolies, curbs on banks, strict environmental controls and conditions on foreign investment.

religion-illusion.rationale: Says men have forgotten God and that the cure for the age is a quest for the warm hand of God.

restrict-private-adult-pornography-acces.rationale: Harvard speech denounces pornography and the boundless freedom granted to it as a symptom of Western moral weakness; he does not give legal remedies.

restrict-technology-exports-to-rivals.rationale: Attacks Western capitalists who sell technology to the Soviet Union and prolong the regime.

revolution-legitimate.rationale: Rejects bloody uprising and revolution: the vileness of the means begets the vileness of the result.

right-to-secede.rationale: Says the twelve non-Slavic republics must be allowed to leave and no one may restrain a separating people by force, with plebiscites in mixed areas.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Says land embodies moral as well as economic values and that a weakening desire to work the land is a danger to the national character.

sacred-nation.rationale: Says nations are the wealth of mankind and each bears a particular facet of God's design.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Wants libraries, museums and heritage protected, and warns against destroying the national past.

second-chamber.rationale: Says the existing two-chamber system with a Chamber of Nationalities would be quite satisfactory if followed honestly.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Laments that state criminals go unpunished and asks at least for a public moral trial of them; no legal scheme.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Says the freedom to seize and gorge oneself is something animals have; human freedom includes self-limitation for others.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Says foreign capital must not set terms and points to the Japanese recovering by work ethic, not foreign infusions.

separate-church-state.rationale: Wants the Church independent of the state and atheism no longer imposed, but also wants a religious basis for public life, not strict separation.

separated-powers.rationale: Questions total separation of the executive, legislative and judicial powers as fragmenting a living state, though he keeps distinct institutions.

simple-living.rationale: Calls for self-limitation, criticises flashy ever-new models and extravagance, and rejects the pursuit of unlimited progress.

single-common-good.rationale: Criticizes party bargaining and professional politicians; wants non-partisan representatives accountable to regions.

single-official-language.rationale: Wants schooling in either language by parents' choice and no forced Russification or Ukrainization.

social-market-economy.rationale: Wants a market economy with state budget for social security, education and housing to soften the transition.

socialized-care.rationale: Wants women able to return to care for their children, with men's wages enough for this.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Wants every presidential prerogative rigorously stipulated by law and the Letter's authoritarianism to rest on law.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Says the West and the East need spiritual renewal and Orthodoxy as the moral basis of the state.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rejects the Marxist doctrine that the state is a class tool and will wither away.

state-harmful.rationale: His whole program in Rebuilding Russia is to build a lawful state order and a strong presidency; he never argues for abolishing the state.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Says the drumming-in of atheism in schools must stop immediately.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Wants the Church independent, free of the state, and the drumming-in of atheism stopped.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Wants free competition of ideas and religions and says to live not by lies.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Says excessive growth in any sector should be held back by antitrust laws and progressive taxation; gives no rates.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Rejects the idea of unlimited progress as the way out and says industrial and technical progress leads to a dead end.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Opposes the empire; wants Russia to give up peripheral nations and focus inward.

total-state.rationale: Wants the state out of religion, art, economy and local life.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Says Soviet communism was worse than Hitler's Germany and condemns it without qualification.

traditional-family.rationale: Says the family has a fundamental role in the salvation of the nation's future and that normal families have ceased to exist under communism.

unions-good.rationale: Praised the AFL-CIO and free trade unions as a defence of workers; the Rebuilding Russia text describes unions only neutrally.

universal-morality.rationale: Asks for moral criteria in politics and says justice means conformity to moral law beyond legal compliance.

vanguard-party.rationale: Rejects communism and a ruling party monopoly.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Wants firm legal limits on concentration of capital and banks not to become hidden masters of all life.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Wants small enterprises encouraged, land sold to working farmers in limited lots and free small plots for workers and townspeople.
